method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia' (published 4 August 2025), 20 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12515471). S2: QUOTED from Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group (Chen W and others), Clinical Hematology International 7(1) (doi 10.46989/001c.133682) 'Consensus Guidelines and Recommendations for The CD38 Monoclonal Antibody-based Quadruplet Therapy and Management in Clinical Practice for Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma: From the Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group' (published 11 April 2025), 10 claims; LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12013828). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the 2025 Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group modified-Delphi consensus on CD38-antibody quadruplets (16 Asia-Pacific experts, GRADE-rated), as the international source showing the quadruplet standard that PBS funding does not yet support. The S1 claims are unchanged. Searched and not usable: EHA-EMN 2025 (Nat Rev Clin Oncol, paywalled), ASCO 2026 living guideline and ASCO-Ontario Health 2026 (bot challenge at ascopubs.org and cancercareontario.ca, not bypassed). EHA-ESMO 2021 (HemaSphere, CC BY) was not used: it predates the quadruplet trials and EHA-EMN 2025 supersedes it.

claims.claim: **Transplant eligibility is an individual judgement:** age, comorbidity, frailty, disability and the patient's wishes all count. Frailty and comorbidity indices can help, but none is validated for this decision.
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Selected fit patients up to age 75 can be transplanted.** Trials mostly capped age at 65, yet data show transplant can be done safely in chosen older patients without a significant rise in transplant-related harm.
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give 3 to 6 induction cycles before transplant, aiming for at least a partial response.** (Grade A, Level II)
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **RVD (lenalidomide, bortezomib, dexamethasone) is the recommended induction for most Australian patients**, because a CD38 antibody is not funded upfront. (Grade A, Level II)
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bortezomib by subcutaneous injection where possible.** A modified **weekly** schedule reduces neuropathy; keep **twice-weekly** dosing for when fast control matters, such as renal failure from cast nephropathy. (Grade B, Level III-3)
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In acute severe renal impairment**, another bortezomib-based regimen (VD, VCD or VTD) can be used for induction instead. (Grade B, Level II)
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **With systemic AL amyloidosis**, where full-dose lenalidomide is poorly tolerated, use **daratumumab with cyclophosphamide, bortezomib and dexamethasone**, which the PBS funds for this. (Grade A, Level II)
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Without a partial response to RVD, the best next step is uncertain.** Proceeding to transplant is reasonable; trials or salvage can be considered, but the PBS funds a new regimen only on proven progression.
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Collect stem cells after 3–4 cycles of RVD, whether transplant is planned now or deferred.** (Grade A, Level II)
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Three ways to mobilise:** G-CSF (10 mcg/kg) on its own; G-CSF plus plerixafor; or G-CSF plus cyclophosphamide (1.5–2 g/m²). When chemotherapy is part of it, choose the **intermediate** cyclophosphamide range over high doses (>2 g/m²): yields are much the same. (Grade B, Level III-3)
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use plerixafor when G-CSF alone or cyclophosphamide with G-CSF fails;** the PBS funds it only after failed chemo-mobilisation. (Grade B, Level II)
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Melphalan 200 mg/m² for patients with normal kidney function.** Consider 140 mg/m² when eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73m². If a patient is judged unfit for 200 mg/m², reconsider whether transplant is appropriate at all.
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Upfront transplant after induction is still the standard of care.** Deferral is reasonable in standard-risk disease, because overall survival was equal in both major trials.
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tandem (second) transplant may still suit eligible high-risk patients, particularly with del17p;** consider it in young high-risk patients, then give maintenance.
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consolidation has uncertain benefit.** Discuss it; offering it is reasonable if induction was well tolerated and there is no peripheral neuropathy.
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Lenalidomide maintenance improves survival and is standard after transplant.** Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Warn patients about second cancers**, especially after 2–3 years from transplant, and keep up age-appropriate cancer screening.
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In Australia, dual maintenance is not funded,** so lenalidomide stays the standard even in high-risk disease.
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess response 3 months after transplant.** Bone marrow biopsy is needed to confirm complete response. MRD testing is possible but not funded in Australia.
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Allogeneic transplant has a limited role outside trials;** if considered, it belongs in an experienced centre.
claims.locator: Medical and Scientific Advisory Group (MSAG) of Myeloma Australia, Internal Medicine Journal, 'Management of patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation: position statement of the Medical and Scientific Advisory Group of Myeloma Australia', published 4 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515471/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **International consensus: a CD38 antibody added to VRd or KRd is suitable first-line treatment for transplant-eligible patients** (evidence A, strong; 92.9% of the panel agreed). NCCN v1.2025 now makes D-VRd its only preferred transplant-eligible regimen, with Isa-VRd as another option. In Australia a CD38 antibody is not PBS-funded upfront, so RVD stays the funded standard (S1).
claims.source_text: CD38 monoclonal antibodies plus VRd/KRd are suitable as a first-line treatment for transplantation-eligible NDMM patients (A1). … In the NCCN Guidelines Version 1.2025, the D-VRd regimen has been updated from an "other recommended option" to the only preferred regimen for NDMM patients eligible for transplant. … 92.9% (13) agree
claims.locator: Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group (Chen W and others), Clinical Hematology International 7(1) (doi 10.46989/001c.133682), 'Consensus Guidelines and Recommendations for The CD38 Monoclonal Antibody-based Quadruplet Therapy and Management in Clinical Practice for Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma: From the Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group', published 11 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12013828/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **PERSEUS (D-VRd v VRd, induction and consolidation around transplant):** complete response or better 87.9% v 70.1%, MRD negativity 75.2% v 47.5%, and 48-month PFS 84.3% v 67.7% (HR 0.42). Grade 3–4 adverse events were more frequent (91.5% v 85.6%), but fewer patients stopped for them (8.8% v 21.3%).
claims.source_text: The D-VRd group demonstrated significantly higher rates of CR or better (87.9% vs. 70.1%, P < 0.001) and MRD negativity (75.2% vs. 47.5%, P < 0.001) compared to the VRd group. At a median follow-up of 47.5 months, the estimated 48-month PFS was 84.3% in the D-VRd group and 67.7% in the VRd group, with a statistically significant HR of 0.42. … grade 3-4 AEs was 91.5% in the D-VRd group, higher than the 85.6% observed in the VRd group. … However, the treatment discontinuation rate due to AEs was lower in the D-VRd group (8.8%) than in the VRd group (21.3%).
claims.locator: Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group (Chen W and others), Clinical Hematology International 7(1) (doi 10.46989/001c.133682), 'Consensus Guidelines and Recommendations for The CD38 Monoclonal Antibody-based Quadruplet Therapy and Management in Clinical Practice for Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma: From the Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group', published 11 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12013828/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Isatuximab quadruplets:** in GMMG-HD7, adding isatuximab to VRd raised post-induction MRD negativity (50% v 36%) with no new safety signals but more neutropenia; in IsKia, Isa-KRd beat KRd on MRD negativity after consolidation (77% v 67%).
claims.source_text: with 50% of patients in the Isa-VRd group achieving MRD negativity compared to 36% in the VRd group (OR 1.82 … From a safety perspective, addition of isatuximab to VRd did not lead to new safety signals. In both treatment groups, the rates of discontinuation due to AEs were low. On the other hand, neutropenia was more frequently seen in the Isa-VRd group … After consolidation, the MRD negativity rates at a sensitivity threshold of 10-5 were 77% in the Isa-KRd group compared to 67% in the KRd group
claims.locator: Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group (Chen W and others), Clinical Hematology International 7(1) (doi 10.46989/001c.133682), 'Consensus Guidelines and Recommendations for The CD38 Monoclonal Antibody-based Quadruplet Therapy and Management in Clinical Practice for Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma: From the Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group', published 11 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12013828/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **High-risk disease and stem-cell collection:** for high-risk patients on CD38-antibody quadruplet induction planned for tandem transplant, plan collection before the fourth cycle, with early plerixafor for poor mobilisers (evidence B, strong; 71.4% agreed).
claims.source_text: For HRMM patients receiving anti-CD38-based quadruplet induction therapy combined with tandem ASCT, stem cell collection should ideally be planned before the fourth cycle, with early plerixafor administration for patients with poor stem cell mobilization. … 71.4% (10) agree
claims.locator: Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group (Chen W and others), Clinical Hematology International 7(1) (doi 10.46989/001c.133682), 'Consensus Guidelines and Recommendations for The CD38 Monoclonal Antibody-based Quadruplet Therapy and Management in Clinical Practice for Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma: From the Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group', published 11 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12013828/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Is a second transplant worth it after a quadruplet?** S2 calls the benefit debatable, because in IFM 2018-04 MRD negativity improved only slightly. S1 still suggests tandem transplant for young high-risk patients; both are shown.
claims.source_text: However, the substantial benefit of a second transplant after a quadruplet therapy incorporating anti-CD38 antibodies may still be debatable, considering the MRD negativity rate were improved only slightly in the IFM 2018-04 trial.
claims.locator: Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group (Chen W and others), Clinical Hematology International 7(1) (doi 10.46989/001c.133682), 'Consensus Guidelines and Recommendations for The CD38 Monoclonal Antibody-based Quadruplet Therapy and Management in Clinical Practice for Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma: From the Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group', published 11 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12013828/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Maintenance:** lenalidomide stays the cornerstone after induction and transplant. S2 adds that lenalidomide plus a CD38 antibody may be considered for high-risk cytogenetics or MRD negativity after quadruplet induction (evidence B, strong; 85.7% agreed), citing AURIGA's higher MRD negativity with D-R; NCCN v1.2025 moved KR and D-R to 'other recommended'. In Australia dual maintenance is not funded (S1).
claims.source_text: Additionally, lenalidomide remains the cornerstone of maintenance therapy following induction and ASCT, and a more aggressive maintenance strategy involving lenalidomide plus anti-CD38 isatuximab or daratumumab may be considered in patients with high-risk cytogenetic abnormalities or those who achieved MRD negativity with their initial quadruplet therapy (B1). … In the phase III AURIGA trial, anti-CD38 naïve post-transplant patients were randomized to receive either daratumumab plus lenalidomide (D-R) or lenalidomide (R) as maintenance treatment. In this study, a higher MRD negativity was achieved in the D-R maintenance group, suggesting that incorporating anti-CD38 in the maintenance therapy could be beneficial. … Additionally, the NCCN Guidelines Version 1.2025 have reclassified the KR and D-R maintenance regimens from "useful in certain circumstances" to "other recommended regimens." … Level of Consensus on that lenalidomide remains the cornerstone of maintenance therapy following induction and ASCT, and a more aggressive maintenance strategy involving lenalidomide plus anti-CD38 may be considered in patients with high-risk cytogenetic abnormalities or those who achieved MRD negativity with their initial quadruplet therapy 85.7% (12) agree
claims.locator: Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group (Chen W and others), Clinical Hematology International 7(1) (doi 10.46989/001c.133682), 'Consensus Guidelines and Recommendations for The CD38 Monoclonal Antibody-based Quadruplet Therapy and Management in Clinical Practice for Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma: From the Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group', published 11 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12013828/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Adverse events:** quadruplets raise grade 3 or higher infections (RR 1.34) and thrombocytopenia (RR 1.39), mostly mild overall, without more anaemia, neuropathy or pneumonia. Manage cytopenias with regular blood counts, dose changes and G-CSF (evidence A, strong). G-CSF prophylaxis fits a febrile-neutropenia risk of 20% or more, 10–20% with extra factors such as age over 65 or frailty, or regimens with neutropenia above 50% (lenalidomide combinations).
claims.source_text: Grade ≥3 AEs that were more common with quadruplet regimens were infections (relative risk [RR] 1.34; 95% CI: 1.17- 1.54) and thrombocytopenia (RR 1.39; 95% CI: 1.12-1.74). Notably, the analysis did not show an increased risk for anemia, neuropathy, or pneumonia at any grade. … Management involving routine complete blood count (CBC) monitoring, dose adjustments, or granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) support are recommended (A1). … While G-CSF prophylaxis is not routinely used in multiple myeloma, it is advised for patients undergoing regimens with a high (≥ 20%) risk of febrile neutropenia, those with intermediate risk (10-20%) who have additional factors (e.g., age > 65 years, frailty), or those on treatments with a neutropenia rate over 50% (e.g., lenalidomide-based combinations).
claims.locator: Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group (Chen W and others), Clinical Hematology International 7(1) (doi 10.46989/001c.133682), 'Consensus Guidelines and Recommendations for The CD38 Monoclonal Antibody-based Quadruplet Therapy and Management in Clinical Practice for Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma: From the Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group', published 11 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12013828/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Before starting a quadruplet:** antiviral (aciclovir or valaciclovir) and antibacterial (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole) prophylaxis, plus influenza and pneumococcal vaccination (evidence A, strong), with vaccination of close contacts too. Consider immunoglobulin replacement if IgG is below 400 mg/dL or there is specific antibody failure; itraconazole raises lenalidomide exposure.
claims.source_text: Quadruplet regimens may increase the infection susceptibility. Therefore, prophylactic antiviral (e.g., acyclovir or valacyclovir) and antibacterial agents (e.g., trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole), and vaccination against influenza and pneumococcal infections are advised prior to initiating quadruplet therapy (A1). … In addition to vaccinating the patients themselves, community immunization is strongly advocated, where close contacts, including family members living with the patient, are also vaccinated. … Polyclonal immunoglobulin (Ig) replacement may be considered for patients with IgG less than 400 mg/dL or specific antibody failure. … particularly with lenalidomide, whose exposure increases when combined with itraconazole, heightening toxicity risk.
claims.locator: Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group (Chen W and others), Clinical Hematology International 7(1) (doi 10.46989/001c.133682), 'Consensus Guidelines and Recommendations for The CD38 Monoclonal Antibody-based Quadruplet Therapy and Management in Clinical Practice for Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma: From the Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group', published 11 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12013828/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Carfilzomib quadruplets (Isa-KRd):** baseline echocardiography and cardiac biomarkers (troponin, NT-proBNP), regular blood pressure checks, and repeat echo if heart failure is suspected.
claims.source_text: Management strategies for cardiovascular AEs include pre-treatment cardiac evaluation with echocardiography and cardiac biomarkers (e.g., troponin, NT-proBNP) to establish a baseline. During treatment, patients should be monitored for symptoms like dyspnea, chest pain, edema, or fatigue to detect potential cardiac dysfunction. Blood pressure should be assessed regularly, especially for patients on Isa-KRd. … If cardiac dysfunction is suspected, further echocardiography is recommended.
claims.locator: Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group (Chen W and others), Clinical Hematology International 7(1) (doi 10.46989/001c.133682), 'Consensus Guidelines and Recommendations for The CD38 Monoclonal Antibody-based Quadruplet Therapy and Management in Clinical Practice for Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma: From the Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group', published 11 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12013828/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **CD38 antibodies and neuropathy:** infusion reactions are common but usually mild and at the first infusion (72.4% in GRIFFIN). If neuropathy threatens treatment, switching bortezomib from twice-weekly to once-weekly keeps Isa-VRd viable.
claims.source_text: For example, in the GRIFFIN trial, IRRs occurred in 72.4% patients and were generally mild, with most patients experiencing them during their first infusion. … adjusting the bortezomib dose from twice-weekly to once-weekly, with regular assessment for neuropathy can still make quadruplet therapy with Isa-VRd a viable option.
claims.locator: Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group (Chen W and others), Clinical Hematology International 7(1) (doi 10.46989/001c.133682), 'Consensus Guidelines and Recommendations for The CD38 Monoclonal Antibody-based Quadruplet Therapy and Management in Clinical Practice for Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma: From the Pan-Pacific Multiple Myeloma Working Group', published 11 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12013828/, retrieved 2026-09-24
